Brief: Write the landing page copy for `sackview`, following the tool page section order.

<<<DRAFT A
# See what is inside a ZIP before you unpack it

sackview lists archive entries and their sizes so you can check the contents before extracting elsewhere.

```sh
pipx install sackview
```

ZIP archives only · Offline inspection · No extraction or archive changes

## Inspect an archive

```sh
sackview inspect photos.zip
```

Each entry shows its name, compressed size, and unpacked size.

## Commands

| Command | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `sackview inspect photos.zip` | All entries in the archive |
| `sackview inspect photos.zip --largest 10` | The ten entries with the largest unpacked sizes, largest first |
| `sackview inspect photos.zip --find '*.csv'` | Only entries whose names match the pattern |

## Keys

Key bindings are not specified.

## Check disk space before extracting

sackview displays the total unpacked size. Use this total to check available disk space before extracting elsewhere.

## Good to know

ZIP support
: Other archive formats produce an unsupported-format message and return exit code 24.

Archive protection
: sackview never extracts entries or changes the archive.

Offline inspection
: Inspection works offline and sends no archive contents to a service.
DRAFT A>>>

<<<DRAFT B
# See inside a ZIP before you unpack it

sackview shows what is inside a ZIP archive before you unpack it. It displays the total unpacked size so you can check available disk space before extracting elsewhere.

Install sackview:

```sh
pipx install sackview
```

Each entry shows its name, compressed size, and unpacked size.

## Inspect an archive

List the entries in `photos.zip`:

```sh
sackview inspect photos.zip
```

## Commands

Show the ten entries with the largest unpacked sizes, largest first:

```sh
sackview inspect photos.zip --largest 10
```

Show only entries whose names match `*.csv`:

```sh
sackview inspect photos.zip --find '*.csv'
```

## Good to know

### Archive safety

sackview never extracts entries or changes the archive.

### Privacy

Inspection works offline and sends no archive contents to a service.

### Supported formats

sackview supports ZIP archives only. Other archive formats produce an unsupported-format message and return exit code 24.

items.title: Thinking
items.text:
I'm weighing two drafts. Draft A follows the expected section order and includes a "Keys" section that feels like filler for a CLI tool. Draft B moves the entry-naming note out of place and drops both the Keys section and the disk-space task, folding the latter into the lead.

Weighing both drafts again, Draft A has the placeholder line about key bindings, which reads like careless template filler on a landing page. Draft B has its own sloppiness, with a stray sentence sitting under the install section. Reading it as a user, both work, though A's table is clearer and it keeps the disk-space section. On balance I still lean toward A, because it follows the expected section order and feels more complete, even with that placeholder flaw.
